sheet-1.description: Sheet 56 of the Sanborn atlas covering Woodridge (today Wood-Ridge) and Moonachie in Bergen County, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. It shows the centre of Woodridge from Hillcrest Avenue at the top down to the double track of the New Jersey and New York Railroad near the bottom, and from Anderson Avenue at the left edge to Willow Avenue near the right edge. North Avenue, Woodridge Avenue, Columbia Boulevard and Highland Avenue run down from Hillcrest Avenue to Hackensack, which crosses the sheet as a curving through road; below it Moonachie runs south through a grid of short cross streets: Washington, Madison, Columbia, Woodridge Street, Jefferson and Monroe. East of Moonachie the blocks along Ryerson, Way and Cliff are largely open, and the large lots east of Highland Avenue and north of Hackensack are almost empty. Most buildings are small frame dwellings with outbuildings and garages. Named premises include a garage at Hackensack and Moonachie, the Woodridge Club, a plumbing and heating shop, H. Bockhaus's machine shop, the Adelung Hotel and Woodridge Station by the railroad, and two florists with long glass-roofed greenhouses: Paul Fischer, east of Moonachie near the railroad, and a larger range in block 106 east of Willow Avenue, which sheet 57 names as Madsen and Christenson. Below the railroad, a strip between Moonachie and Division Avenue lies along the Woodridge and Moonachie borough line. Water pipes and their sizes are drawn in the streets, and numbers of adjoining sheets (54, 55, 57, 59) mark the margins.
notes: Willow Av. is today Windsor Road (OpenStreetMap); the Willow on sheet 57 is a different street.
Washington, between Hackensack and Madison at Anderson Avenue, is today Hill Street.
Hackensack is today Hackensack Street; Moonachie is Moonachie Avenue; Ryerson is Ryerson Avenue.
Monroe and the Division Avenue shown here were not matched to a modern street and were not used as control.
The railroad is lettered N.J. & N.Y. R.R.; today the Pascack Valley Line.

Printed sheet 56 (Bergen County volume page), 100 ft to an inch, one part, whole sheet. Wood-Ridge between Hillcrest Av. and the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad, Anderson Av. to Willow Av. (now Windsor Road); the greenhouses east of Willow Av. repeat on sheet 57 part 2. Turned on the page: north about 53 degrees clockwise of up.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 57, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right, covering the western part of Moonachie at its border with Woodridge. A boundary line marked Woodridge and Moonachie runs along Bergen near the top; above it, a strip of Woodridge blocks next to the railroad repeats the bottom of sheet 56. Below, a regular grid of cross streets, Bergen, Oak, Union, Concord and Willow, is cut by Anderson Avenue on the left, Moonachie Avenue in the middle and Division Avenue to the right. Building is sparse: scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings along Anderson and Moonachie Avenues, with the blocks east of Division Avenue laid out in lots but almost wholly empty. Public School No. 2 stands on Moonachie Avenue between Union and Concord, and fire gongs are marked at street corners. Below Willow the drawing opens into undivided ground crossed by Berry's Creek, which Moonachie Avenue crosses on a concrete bridge; a large compass rose sits in the open area to the left, and a dash-dot match line marked A and B leads to the lower right part of the sheet. A second Woodridge and Moonachie borough line runs down the left side beside Anderson Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in most streets. The part is bounded at the bottom by heavy lines that separate it from the two lower parts of the sheet.
notes: Bergen is today Berger Street (OpenStreetMap); its junctions carry residuals of about 4 to 5 m, so the modern line may be slightly off the old one.
Willow here is today Willow Street, not the Willow Av. of sheet 56.
Division Avenue east of Moonachie Avenue has no modern counterpart in the reference data; the blocks east of it were not used as control.
Public School No. 2 on Moonachie Avenue.

Printed sheet 57, 100 ft to an inch, three parts divided by heavy lines: part 1 main map (Moonachie between Bergen and Willow, Anderson Av. to Division Av., down to Berry's Creek); part 2 lower left (Hackensack Av. and Terrace Av. at the Woodridge / Hasbrouck Heights line, overlapping the east edge of sheet 56); part 3 lower right (Grant and Romeo, Moonachie, drawn about 7 degrees more turned than part 1).

sheet-2-2.description: The lower left part of sheet 57, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right and set off from the rest of the sheet by heavy lines. It shows a strip along Hackensack Avenue, which becomes Terrace Avenue where it crosses the borough line between Woodridge and Hasbrouck Heights, with Lincoln Avenue running north from Terrace Avenue. The ground north of the avenue is marked as shown on sheet 59, and its west end overlaps the east edge of sheet 56. South of the avenue, in block 106, are the greenhouses of Madsen and Christenson, florists: a range of long glass-roofed houses with a packing house, office and wagon shed, hydrants and hose noted. East of the borough line stand the Hasbrouck Heights Embroidery Works, with notes on its power, heating, lighting and water supply, and a few frame dwellings. A 12 inch water pipe runs in Hackensack and Terrace Avenues. The rest of the part is open ground. The sheet's scale bar is printed at the bottom.
notes: Hackensack Av. is today Hackensack Street; it becomes Terrace Avenue at the borough line, as on the sheet.
Placed from one junction (Lincoln Avenue / Terrace Avenue) and two points carried from sheet 56 (the greenhouse corner and a dwelling), which draws the same block.

Printed sheet 57, 100 ft to an inch, three parts divided by heavy lines: part 1 main map (Moonachie between Bergen and Willow, Anderson Av. to Division Av., down to Berry's Creek); part 2 lower left (Hackensack Av. and Terrace Av. at the Woodridge / Hasbrouck Heights line, overlapping the east edge of sheet 56); part 3 lower right (Grant and Romeo, Moonachie, drawn about 7 degrees more turned than part 1).

sheet-2-3.description: The lower right part of sheet 57, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the main part by a heavy line and turned a few degrees further, with its own north arrow. It continues the main part to the south east, into the centre of Moonachie, and is labelled Moonachie. Anderson Avenue on the left and Moonachie Avenue on the right are crossed by Grant and Romeo, which enclose block 22; block 23 lies below Romeo and blocks 19 and 20 above Grant and east of Moonachie Avenue. Buildings are scattered frame dwellings with sheds and stables. On the east side of Moonachie Avenue stand a hall and the fire department hose house, with a hose cart and 500 feet of hose noted, and a fire gong at the corner across the avenue. Moonachie Avenue bends to the south east at the bottom of the part. Much of the ground is open, and the corners outside the mapped blocks are marked 0 as not shown elsewhere.
notes: Grant / Moonachie Avenue is drawn about 20 m further north than the modern Grand Street junction and was not used; the part rests on three junctions with no redundancy.
